question.question: Can VerifyLeader complete successfully using nonvoter worker support after this peer has lost effective leadership to a newer elected voter leader, and do the lease and negative-response paths prevent that outcome in a permitted execution?
question.importance: VerifyLeader explicitly supports avoiding stale FSM reads after leadership loss. If nonvoters can supply sufficient verification support while the voter majority elects elsewhere, callers could treat an obsolete authority observation as permission to return stale data. This consequence requires an actual replacement-leader history and endpoint observation; code asymmetry alone does not establish it.
contexts: Stable protocol-v3 configuration containing voters and a nonvoter
One pending verification in an old leader tenure
Permitted transport partition/delay and real election in the voter component

Successful nonvoter reply -> notifyAll(true) -> vote(true) -> threshold -> leaderLoop future completion
Voter majority election competes with old leader lease expiry, negative reply and leader-session cleanup

question.trigger_rationale: Initial two-line trace found an eligibility mismatch at a concrete A2 consumer: B-verify-consume turns scalar positive worker support into public leadership assurance, although B-verify-register enrolls nonvoters and F-verify-support carries no voter eligibility. Next discriminator is a real-worker, stable-membership partition history with observed new election and old VerifyLeader return, not direct assignment of authority state.

feedback.answered: Initial source investigation connects client command formation, qualified log support, authority acquisition/loss, membership, recovery and application. Log commitment and lease count voters; pending leadership verification is registered with every replication worker. This is a distinct authority-support question, with protective lease, negative replies and tenure cleanup retained.

feedback.rationale: Compared three directions: verification eligibility has a direct public contract and tractable in-memory real-worker schedule; heartbeat/term asymmetry requires blocked-progress timing and a more precise lease consequence; partial vote persistence needs a concrete permitted storage failure contract. Select verification eligibility first because it can distinguish authority-consumption behavior without claiming broader log safety. The other sourced surfaces remain open.
